newsitem.title: UK: British MP to sue paper over gay allegation.
newsitem.headline: British MP to sue paper over gay allegation.

text.p: A British member of parliament said by a Sunday tabloid to have had a homosexual affair with a teenaged researcher is to sue the newspaper for libel, the MP's lawyers said on Tuesday.

Jerry Hayes, 43, a member of the ruling Conservative Party, has denied the allegations, printed by the News of the World last Sunday, that he had cheated on his wife during an affair with 18-year-old Paul Stone.

Lawyers Swepstone Walsh said they had "served a writ claiming damages for libel on the publishers of the News of the World on behalf of Jerry Hayes MP in respect of their story concerning Mr Hayes, published on January 5 1997".
The top-selling newspaper's legal manager, Tom Crone, said: "The News of the World has not yet seen the writ which Mr Hayes's solicitors say they have served.
"However, our position is as it was last weekend, that we are satisfied with the accuracy of the story we published."
Prime Minister John Major has sought to place family values at the heart of the Conservative campaign in the leadup to the next general election which must be called by May.
